reflux_why: Touching an ending is heavy on the channels: death is cold, but working it leaves a lot of spent heat behind. High reflux gives Death a reason to keep the corpses it makes: Lay to Rest turns corpses into essence and sheds reflux, the way Backdraft is fire's way down.
rule: What has died stays useful: for a Death fighter every enemy corpse lies 20 s and Death skills spend it, and a living target below half health is Dying and takes 30% more from Death.
rule_why: design/14 named the two halves (corpses are material, below half is prey) but not how long a corpse lasts, how a skill finds one, or what 'prey' does in numbers. Today a corpse lies 8 s (balance.combat.corpse_lie_s); 20 s gives a fight time to use them. Dying is a fixed +30%, the mirror of Life's +25% on the hale, so the two read as opposites. Death skills say plainly whether they need a corpse, and each is checked before essence is spent.

skills.name: Endstroke
skills.summary: One enemy in reach: 2.0x strike damage, 30% more if it is Dying (below half). Anything short of an elite left under 15% of its health dies outright.
skills.verb_fit: Kill is finishing the dying. It is an ordinary blow on a healthy target and a certain one on a failing one.

new_mechanics.name: dying
new_mechanics.definition: Derived, never applied: a living target below half its health. Death hits on it do x1.3 (affinity key dying_mult). Shown as a faint mark over its head while a Death fighter is in the fight.

new_mechanics.name: execute_below
new_mechanics.definition: A strike key: after the hit, a non-elite target whose health is below that fraction of its maximum dies at once (the kill is yours, with every on-kill rule).

new_mechanics.name: corpse
new_mechanics.definition: An enemy's body where it fell. For a character holding Death it lies 20 s instead of balance.combat.corpse_lie_s. Death skills that need one target a corpse within their range (the cursor snaps to the nearest corpse) and are refused, with nothing spent, if there is none. A corpse can be spent once; Lingering Shade does not spend it.

good_modifiers.word: everything into one body: 25% harder
a drawn-back killing blow: 30% harder, 30% longer wind-up
down for good: 30% more poise damage and it interrupts
a furious finish: 20% harder, 10% dearer

bad_modifiers.why: a killing blow that holds the life at the edge. The numbers would land (Spared, 15% weaker) and then the execute can never fire, because a Spared target cannot die; the two verbs cancel.
a finishing blow is on one body. Extra jumps do nothing and fall back; the 15% damage loss lands.

skills.name: Last Mercy
skills.summary: One enemy within 10 m is Spared for 4 s: nothing can take it below 1 health. If it is already below half, it kneels and does nothing. Hold a Censer-Bearer at the edge until it is clear of its friends.
skills.verb_fit: Spare is holding a life at the edge. The target cannot die, and one already failing is held there helpless.

new_mechanics.name: hex
new_mechanics.definition: Defined in blood.json (gullet_knot): a target within range takes on_hit at once, no travel, needs line of sight.

new_mechanics.name: spared
new_mechanics.definition: 1 stack, lasts the skill's duration: the target's health cannot fall below 1 (no death, so no death-burst). If it is Dying it kneels: it cannot move or act. When Spared ends, the next blow can kill it as normal.

good_modifiers.word: a longer mercy: half as long again
spare from 40% further away
spared, and haunted while it waits: Spared and Dreading together
held quite still at the edge: 40% longer, a little dearer

bad_modifiers.why: finishing the life you are holding. Last Mercy deals no damage on a hit, so the bonus has nothing to add to; it falls back to a small cost cut.
rage in a mercy. No damage to raise, so that falls back, and the 10% cost rise lands.

skills.name: Rise Again
skills.summary: Point at a corpse within 10 m: it gets up and fights for you for 15 s, with 120 health, hitting the nearest enemy for 15 a blow. Two at a time. Without a corpse nothing happens and nothing is spent.
skills.verb_fit: Animate is the dead getting up. The corpse is the material; the skill gives it 15 s of use.

new_mechanics.name: summon
new_mechanics.definition: A new kind: spends a corpse and puts a thrall (an ally body using the corpse's model with set_dead_look) at it for duration. A thrall walks to the nearest enemy and strikes; enemies may attack it; it is not living (Life cannot touch it). Its kills are credited to the caster. A third pushes out the oldest.

good_modifiers.word: an embalmed thrall: 40% longer, a little less reflux
the dead stay up half as long again
cheaper: 15% less essence
it remembers how to fight a little longer: 30% longer

bad_modifiers.why: putting down for good what you are raising. The summon has no hit of its own, so the poise and interrupt fall back to a small cost cut; the verbs cancel.
banishing the thing you made. Nothing it hits to interrupt and no damage to raise; both fall back to a small cost cut.

skills.name: Lay to Rest
skills.summary: Every corpse within 6 m of you (up to 4) goes into the ground for good. Each gives you back 5 essence and takes 8 off your death reflux, and the ground drags down the enemies standing next to it: 40 poise damage and interrupted.
skills.verb_fit: Lay is putting the dead down for good. The corpses are gone, nothing can raise them, and what they had left is yours.

new_mechanics.name: field_pulse
new_mechanics.definition: A new kind: acts on the caster's own field pieces (corpses here; growth patches in nature.json) within radius of the caster or of an aimed point. Per piece it pays a reward or a burst, and on_hit lands on enemies within drag_radius of each piece once.

good_modifiers.word: a wider burial: 30% more reach
a quiet burial: 20% less reflux from casting it
the ground pulls harder: 30% more poise damage

bad_modifiers.why: getting the dead up while you put them down. There is no duration or speed here, so both halves fall back to a small cost cut.
a body laid to rest leaves no spirit. Dread would land on whoever the ground drags, but the word contradicts itself; the duration half falls back.

skills.name: Rotting Bolt
skills.summary: A clot of decay thrown along your aim: 50 and Rotting for 6 s (its armour and shield count for half, and lost poise does not come back). If it hits a corpse instead, the corpse bursts: 60 and Rotting to everything within 2.5 m.
skills.verb_fit: Rot is decay. On the living it decays guard and armour; on the dead it decays the whole body at once.

new_mechanics.name: rotting
new_mechanics.definition: 1 stack, 6 s: the target's armour, front armour and front_block count at half, and its poise does not refill.

new_mechanics.name: hits_corpses
new_mechanics.definition: A projectile key: corpses are in its path like bodies; one hit bursts (corpse_burst payload in its radius) and is spent.

good_modifiers.word: rot that goes through: pierces the line, rotting every body and bursting every corpse it crosses
decay that finds the failing: +40% against the Dying
what rots, haunts: Dreading as well as Rotting
thrown 40% further, a little weaker

bad_modifiers.why: stopping the decay the bolt is made of. A projectile has no duration, so that falls back to a small damage bonus; the reflux cut lands.
cleansing the rot. The reflux cut lands; the word contradicts itself.

skills.name: Embalm
skills.summary: For 5 s you cannot die: your health stops at 1, though blows that land still open wounds as usual. You heal nothing while it lasts.
skills.verb_fit: Preserve stops decay, the user's own body included. For five seconds your body will not end.

new_mechanics.name: embalmed
new_mechanics.definition: A self_buff read in take_hit: the bar cannot fall below floor_health; wounds are still added by the wound rules; all healing to the player is refused while it lasts. Nothing happens when it ends (no skill hurts its caster).

good_modifiers.word: preserved half as long again
all on you: 30% longer
cheaper: 15% less essence
the body holds its shape a little longer: 30% longer

bad_modifiers.why: decay put into your own preservation. A self buff hits nobody; Rotting falls back to a small cost cut.
a killing edge on a skill that stops you dying. No damage on a hit, so the bonus falls back to a small cost cut.

skills.name: Lingering Shade
skills.summary: Point at a corpse within 10 m, or where something died in the last 10 s: its shade lingers there for 8 s in a 3 m circle. Enemies inside take 15 a second and are Dreading: they back out and will not walk in. The corpse is left for other uses.
skills.verb_fit: Haunt is what dies lingering as a spirit. The body stays; what lingers is the dead man's shade, and the living fear its ground.

new_mechanics.name: dread
new_mechanics.definition: 1 stack, 1.5 s, refreshed while in the zone: the target moves away from the zone's centre, will not path into it (the zone is a blocked area in its routing), and a ranged enemy inside loses its aim.

good_modifiers.word: the shade lingers half as long again
a wider haunting: 30% larger, a little softer
haunted ground that rots: Rotting as well as Dread
the dead remember longer: 30% longer

bad_modifiers.why: banishing the spirit you called up. The numbers would land (interrupts, 10% harder) but the verbs cancel; the word should not form.
pulling enemies into ground they flee. The pull would land and fight the Dread every tick; the word contradicts itself.

skills.name: Banishing Line
skills.summary: An instant line 10 m long through everything: 55, 20 poise damage, and interrupts. Constructs, spirits and anything animated take triple.
skills.verb_fit: Exorcise banishes spirits and constructs. Against them it is the strongest hit Death has; against the living it is a line that stops what they were doing.

new_mechanics.name: unliving_mult
new_mechanics.definition: A damage multiplier against targets with living false (enemies.json; defined in life.json).

good_modifiers.word: a longer line: 40% more range
a narrower, harder line: 30% harder, 20% shorter
banishing what is failing: +40% against the Dying
it strikes the spirit: 20% more poise damage

bad_modifiers.why: making the spirits it banishes. Dread would land, but the word contradicts itself; a beam has no duration, so that half falls back.
raising what you banish. No duration or speed on a beam; both fall back to a small damage bonus.

skills.name: Gravestep
skills.summary: You pass out of sight and step out up to 6 m away, or up to 12 m away onto a corpse. Every enemy that was aiming at you loses its aim.
skills.verb_fit: Vanish is passing out of sight and reach. You are gone before you are back, and anything taking aim at you has nothing to aim at.

new_mechanics.name: breaks_aim
new_mechanics.definition: A movement key: every enemy winding up a ranged attack on the caster loses it (as interrupt(), without the stagger).

good_modifiers.word: out of reach entirely: 40% further
you step out somewhere else: 30% further
gone sooner: a quarter less recovery
cheaper: 15% less essence

bad_modifiers.why: appearing on the skill that is disappearing. A blink has no damage or poise fields, so both halves fall back to a small cost cut.
the step touches nobody; Rotting falls back to a small cost cut.

skills.name: Death Mask
skills.summary: Point, 8 m: a likeness of you takes form out of grave-dust. For 5 s every enemy within 6 m turns on it instead of you. When it breaks or its time runs out, it falls apart: 40 to everything within 3 m.
skills.verb_fit: Manifest is appearing, taking form. Something that looks like you appears where you are not, and the room believes it.

new_mechanics.name: decoy
new_mechanics.definition: A prop key: while it stands, enemies within radius take it as their target instead of the player (it holds slots like the player); it has hp and blocks nothing. When it breaks or its life ends it deals damage within collapse_radius.

good_modifiers.word: the likeness holds half as long again
it draws from 30% further, and falls apart a little softer
a better-made likeness: 10% harder when it falls
they keep believing it: 30% longer

bad_modifiers.why: a likeness nobody can see draws nobody. The 20% reach would land (it pulls from further) while the word contradicts itself; the prop has no wind-up, so that half falls back.
hiding the thing that must be seen. No wind-up to cut; it falls back to a small damage bonus.
